title: Render and cook cancellation — TOPS cancel, rkill-based render stop, emergency halt (R73 scope)
status_note: Describes what happened (Law 3). All three parts of the brief were built AND demonstrated live on Houdini 22.0.368. PART A: a real /tasks cook was cancelled through the shipped handler, with an uncancelled control proving the same cook runs past 25s untouched. PART B: rkill was demonstrated against real mantra and Karma renders through the shipped module, the RopNode->process mapping was established for Karma and REFUTED for mantra, and the mandatory partial-frame question was probed on both renderers. PART C: emergency halt is surfaced as a distinct overflow control, and probing exposed that the shipped EmergencyProtocol does NOT halt what it claims. _on_stop is byte-for-byte unchanged. Suite 5031 -> 5069 (+38, 0 failed).
settings_profile: harness/relay-settings.json (governing). RECORDED HONESTLY, NOT CLAIMED (per H3a precedent): execution was in an interactive Claude Code session whose grant is wider than that file. No deny-listed path was touched: shared/bridge.py, VERSION, harness/state/**, the constitution and the rulings doc are all unmodified.

findings.claim: A background render CAN be stopped from SYNAPSE, and it now is. R48's 'not-implementable' is refuted by working code, not by argument.
findings.evidence: Shipped module driven end-to-end against live renders: idle ROP -> 'noop_not_rendering'; live Karma render -> pid 23120 mapped to /stage/h3b_usdrender; stop by ROP path -> status 'stopped', killed=True, verified by rps re-read; stopping again -> 'noop_not_rendering'; bogus pid -> 'noop_no_such_pid'.

findings.claim: THE MAPPING IS RENDERER-DEPENDENT, and for mantra it does not exist. Karma/husk renders are attributable to their ROP; mantra renders are not attributable by ANY available field.
findings.karma: rps reports husk's full command line containing usd_renders/usdrender_<houdiniPID>_<node.sessionId()>_<counter>/. Decoded live: ROP sessionId 113 -> usdrender_40868_113_4; sessionId 339 -> usdrender_40868_339_1.
findings.mantra: rps Command is the bare word 'mantra' for every mantra render. The OS command line is ALSO bare 'mantra' (Win32_Process), because Houdini pipes the IFD over stdin (soho_pipecmd='mantra'). Two concurrent mantra renders are indistinguishable.
findings.consequence: render_stop returns status='unmappable' and REFUSES rather than killing the only render running. Demonstrated live: stop by node -> 'unmappable', killed=False; stop by explicit pid -> 'stopped', killed=True.
findings.why_this_is_the_finding: The brief asked for the mapping and said that if it cannot be made reliable, THAT is the deliverable. It is reliable for one renderer and impossible for the other, and shipping a stop that guessed between them is how you kill the wrong render.

findings.claim: MANDATORY FINDING (brief PART B.3). Stopping a MANTRA render leaves a structurally valid but PIXEL-EMPTY EXR at the real output path. It is not corrupt -- it is valid-and-empty, which is worse, because a file-exists or file-parses check passes it.
findings.measured: Mid-render: h3b_mantra.0001.exr = 1,015 bytes + h3b_mantra.0001.exr.mantra_checkpoint = 5,249,684 bytes. After rkill: BOTH unchanged -- the 1,015-byte EXR and the orphaned checkpoint remain. After clean completion: EXR = 49,863 bytes, checkpoint REMOVED.
findings.the_dangerous_part: iinfo -v on the killed frame exits 0 and reports a full, correct 1920x1080 header with EXR magic 762f3101. It parses. It has no pixels.
detectors_both_measured: an orphaned <output>.mantra_checkpoint beside the frame (removed on clean completion)
the EXR header lacks renderTime / renderMemory / date; a completed mantra frame carries all three (observed renderTime=3.157328, renderTime_s='0:00:03.16')
findings.shipped_as: render_stop.partial_output_risk() returns this as DATA with every stop, so a caller cannot receive a clean-looking success without also receiving the residue it must check. Pinned by test_mantra_partial_output_is_declared_UNSAFE and its mutation.

findings.claim: Stopping a KARMA render is SAFE. husk cannot corrupt the declared output because it never writes it until completion.
findings.mechanism: husk writes progressive snapshots to a SEPARATE file <stem>_part.exr and writes the declared output only on completion, removing _part as it goes. The usdrender_rop invokes husk with --snapshot 300.
findings.evidence: Driving husk directly with --snapshot 3, its own log reads verbatim 'Saved Image: .../h3b_snap_part.exr' repeatedly during the render; on completion h3b_snap.exr exists (2,378,855 bytes) and h3b_snap_part.exr is GONE. A Karma render killed mid-flight produced NO file at its declared output path at all. Killed husk temp dirs were cleaned up.

findings.claim: rkill is SILENT on both success and no-match, so it can never be its own receipt.
findings.evidence: hou.hscript('rkill zzz_no_such_render_h3b') -> out='', err=''. hou.hscript('rkill 72712') -> out='', err='' -- and the process WAS killed (tasklist confirmed dead).
findings.consequence: Every stop in render_stop.py is verified by re-reading rps, and the status 'kill_unconfirmed' exists specifically for the case where rkill was issued and the PID is still live. Law 3: a status that reported the ISSUING of rkill would be reporting an attempt, not an outcome.
findings.second_instrument_note: rps retains ended renders as rows with PID -1; they are excluded from every mapping and are never returned as kill targets (pinned + mutation-proved, M1).

findings.claim: EmergencyProtocol.trigger_emergency_halt DOES NOT HALT WHAT IT CLAIMS. It returns action='ALL_OPERATIONS_HALTED' while the cook it was asked to stop keeps running.
findings.measured: With a real cook in flight at /tasks/h3b_topnet (ctx.cooking=True), trigger_emergency_halt returned action='ALL_OPERATIONS_HALTED' in 0.0 s and ctx.cooking was STILL True at every 0.5s sample through t=3.0s.
findings.root_cause: shared/bridge.py:2288 walks hou.node('/obj').allSubChildren() ONLY. TOP networks live under /tasks by default, so the shipped halt misses the common case entirely. Its 'action' key is a string literal, not a state change, and the whole hou walk is inside try/except: pass.
findings.why_it_matters: This was one step from shipping as my Emergency-halt button -- the exact R18 defect: an affordance claiming a safety action it does not perform. It was caught only because the control was probed against a real cook instead of being wired and assumed.
findings.what_was_done: shared/bridge.py is DENY-LISTED, so the function was not edited. Instead _handle_emergency_halt reports three things separately and never merges them: bridge_halt (what EmergencyProtocol itself did, /obj scope, with the measurement quoted inline), topnets_cancelled (a scene-wide sweep the handler then performs via hou.TopNode.cancelCook -- the verb H3a-F2 found unused), and renders_still_running (deliberately NOT killed). status is 'halted' only when nothing survived, else 'halted_partial'.
findings.verified_after: The handler's sweep, run against the SAME cook that defeated the shipped halt: ctx.cooking False at t=0.5s and every sample after; topnets_cancelled=['/tasks/h3b_topnet'], failures none.

findings.claim: My own reader had an untested branch, and the mutation harness found it -- not review.
findings.detail: Mutation M6 ('reader returns a default target instead of None') initially SURVIVED: 35/35 pins still green. Cause: the negative control used VALID json, which returns None from an earlier branch and never reaches the mutated line. The truncated-with-no-node path -- the one a real cook produces -- had no control at all. A reader that invented '/tasks/topnet1' as a fallback would have passed every pin and cancelled the wrong network.
findings.fixed: Added test_reader_returns_None_for_a_TRUNCATED_payload_with_no_node and test_reader_refuses_a_file_path_as_a_node_target; tightened the fallback to decline file-looking paths (a truncated payload can hide the node key while leaving an output path visible). M6 and a new M7 now both go red.
findings.second_order: When M6's anchor went stale after the repair, the harness reported 'anchor not found -- this result proves nothing' rather than a green. That is the harness obeying Law 1 about itself.

findings.claim: What this stop does NOT cover, stated rather than implied.
findings.foreground_renders: A foreground/in-process render never becomes a background process, never appears in rps, and cannot be reached. Related and unchanged: CHANGELOG.md:27's head-of-line blocking on the WS /synapse path still applies to that transport. The panel's new controls use the HTTP /mcp path (tool_executor.try_mcp_tool_call), and both demonstrations above ran while the cook/render was in flight.
findings.ipr: hou.IPRViewer.killRender EXISTS and is a DIFFERENT case -- interactive preview, not a ROP render. Noted and left there, per brief PART B.4. Not wrapped.
findings.wildcard: 'rkill *' kills every background render on the host including renders this session never started. Deliberately unreachable from render_stop.
findings.license: Probed on Houdini Indie. mantra and husk both spawn and both appear in rps on this license; no Indie-specific limitation was observed for either. A commercial license was not tested and no claim is made about it.

findings.claim: A wrong result was one report away from shipping, and re-running rather than reporting is what caught it.
findings.detail: The first selective-kill test showed BOTH renders gone after rkill on one PID, which reads as 'rkill is not PID-selective' -- a finding that would have made a per-ROP stop impossible and changed the leg's whole conclusion. Re-run with separated outputs and tight timing: the target died inside 0.5s and the OTHER render stayed alive across a full 5s watch. The first run's survivor had simply finished naturally, having been running far longer.
findings.recorded_because: Article VI -- the drift log is the record of the instrument being wrong. The false version is preserved in the evidence artifact under false_start_recorded so no future reader re-derives it.

for_ruling.question: EmergencyProtocol.trigger_emergency_halt is defective in shared/bridge.py, which is deny-listed. Who repairs it, and is the handler-side compensation the permanent answer or a stopgap?
for_ruling.context: H3b-F6: it walks /obj only, misses /tasks entirely, sets action='ALL_OPERATIONS_HALTED' as a literal regardless of what happened, and wraps its only real work in except: pass. This leg compensated in the handler because it could not edit the file. That leaves TWO halt implementations with different scopes, which is its own drift risk. The clean fix is a scene-wide sweep inside bridge.py and an action string derived from what was actually cancelled.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Assigns work behind a deny fence, and choosing between 'fix the bridge' and 'keep the compensation' is a value judgement about where the halt's authority lives. Article I.

for_ruling.question: Should SYNAPSE record the render PID at spool time so MANTRA renders become mappable?
for_ruling.context: H3b-F2: mantra is unmappable from rps because its command carries no identity. But SYNAPSE could snapshot rps immediately before and after ITS OWN render call and attribute the new PID to the ROP it just launched -- the differential approach. It would work only for renders SYNAPSE starts, and it carries a race: a second render starting inside the same window would be misattributed. The alternative is the current honest refusal.
for_ruling.why_escalated: A defensible-either-way trade between coverage and the risk of killing the wrong render. The cost of being wrong is an artist's 40-minute render. Not an agent's call.

for_ruling.question: Do the harness notes that still carry the over-broad 'Houdini exposes NO API to cancel a render' claim get corrected, or preserved as historical record?
for_ruling.context: harness/notes/receipts/H3a.json:89 is the strongest surviving instance and it is now REFUTED. It is a receipt, and receipts are supposed to be the immutable record of what a leg found; editing one retroactively is its own hazard. R73 already corrects it in the rulings doc. Also open: harness/notes/H3a_SIDEFX_ASK.md carries the superseded ask (docs/SIDEFX_ASK_H22_DRAFT.md is the corrected one).
for_ruling.why_escalated: Amending a completed leg's receipt is a governance question, not an engineering one.

for_ruling.question: Should the panel's Cancel-cook control be reachable while the tool detail carries no node -- e.g. by asking Houdini directly which TOP network is cooking?
for_ruling.context: The control is currently gated on the panel knowing a node path, recovered from a truncated tool-status string. When it does not know, it refuses (H3b-F7 is why that refusal is not negotiable). A scene-wide 'cancel whatever is cooking' would always be available but removes the artist's certainty about WHAT gets cancelled -- the same class of trade as H3b-R2. The emergency-halt control already offers the scene-wide version, which may make this moot.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Product-direction judgement about how much the panel should infer on the artist's behalf.
